newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian shares close down in flat trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian shares close down in flat trade.

text.p: Blue chips at Indian exchanges drifted lower to end with small losses on Wednesday with little action seen ahead of a local Bombay holiday, dealers said.
"People don't want to make fresh purchases at these levels. The market is clearly in a consolidation stage," said Nand Kishore Gupta, chief executive at Ind-Sec Share & Stock Broking.

The lack of any major market-moving news kept prices in range bound trade and an anticipated hike in prices of petroleum products and a corruption scandal involving Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's Janata Dal party chief Laloo Prasad Yadav kept buyers to the sidelines, traders said.
"The market is now in a neutral to overbought zone," said Prateek Agrawal, deputy manager research at SBI Capital Markets.
"Though the bellwether stocks are expected to see a correction, it is the second rung stocks which should be the leaders in the future rally," Agrawal said in a report.

More than 3.5 million shares of Bank of India were traded on the first day of listing at the National Stock Exchange on Wednesday. Shares of the state-run bank closed 4.30 rupees higher at 66.80 from its opening on the National exchange.
Shares in the bank, which made a 6.67 billion rupee share issue at 45 rupees, rose 6.0 to 66.75 at the Bombay exchange.
"Action is slowly shifting from the top stocks," Ind-Sec's Gupta said. Select sugar shares had notched gains with analysts predicting a turnaround in the sugar industry, Gupta added.
Shares of Century Textiles and Industries Ltd plunged for the second straight day on Wednesday after the diversified firm announced a 99 percent fall in net profit, traders said.
The share lost 225.75 rupees, or nearly 10 percent, to end at 2,033.25 the day's lowest levels at the Bombay exchange.
Century Textiles hit the BSE's daily price limit of 10 percent, otherwise it might have fallen further.
The National exchange's 50-stock index lost 4.0 points to 1,044.40. The Bombay exchange is closed on Thursday for a local holiday, but other Indian exchange will remain open.
